evidenceStatus: Deterministic model outputs under illustrative inputs; not empirical estimates of realized organizational effects.

sources.timeCost: Step durations: legal minima (PZP 2019 + Dyrektywa 2014/24/UE) and practitioner benchmarks — not a single empirical source
sources.opportunityCost: Deployment-delay cost = procurement duration × daily cost of inaction (model construction)
sources.productivityCost: Szucs (2024), JEEA 22(1):117–160, DOI 10.1093/jeea/jvad017: discretion increased normalized prices by about 6 percentage points and selected firms with about 28% lower measured productivity in the corrected main specification. The model monetizes price only and stress-tests 2–9%; Hungarian public-procurement transfer caveat applies
sources.renegotiationCost: Beuve, Moszoro & Spiller (2023), JLEO 39(1):281–308, DOI 10.1093/jleo/ewab039: 2SLS/IV estimate for annual formal-amendment frequency, not event probability, in French car-park contracts. The model maps 0–0.105 additional amendments per contract-year to a separate contract-rigidity profile and multiplies by contract duration and user-supplied per-amendment cost
sources.tcoCost: Scenario assumption only: a three-year cumulative non-acquisition lifecycle savings pool is stress-tested at 0–15%, scaled by min(horizon years / 3, 1), and multiplied by path-specific capture rates. The central case is zero because no transferable empirical estimate is available
sources.bypassCost: Scenario assumption only: illustrative bypass-rate range, scaled by system controls. Lipsky (1980), Vaughan (1996), and Holmström & Milgrom (1991) support mechanisms, not probabilities
